target_customer: Car owners in the San Francisco Bay Area who want repairs without visiting a shop
problem: Car repair is inconvenient and opaque. CarDash picked up the car, managed the repair at partner shops and returned it with upfront pricing.
business_model: managed marketplace taking a margin on repair services

founders.name: Yinon Weiss
founders.background_notes: No background on the YC page.

technical_complexity.rationale: Booking and logistics software; the hard parts were operations, shop partnerships and unit economics.

defensibility.rationale: Valet and shop partnerships were operational and could be replicated; no data or network advantage reported.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: RepairSmith acquired CarDash in February 2020 to fold its technology into its own offering; terms undisclosed.

market_need_then: A TechCrunch 2017 article covered CarDash's 5.3 million dollar funding as it tried to change car servicing; consumer convenience demand in on-demand services was high but repair margins are thin.

branding.domain_note: Website field points to repairsmith.com, which now redirects to autonationmobileservice.com.

rebrands.why: RepairSmith acquired CarDash and served its customers through RepairSmith.com.

brand_strength.rationale: Launch press (TechCrunch, PYMNTS) but no brand-specific coverage; the name resembles DoorDash style names and is generic.

outcome_analysis: CarDash raised a 5.3 million dollar seed in 2017 for managed car repair with valet pickup but no later round was found. RepairSmith, a Daimler backed mobile repair company, acquired it in February 2020 without disclosed terms. The cause of the stall is not public; the failure tags are inferred from the absence of later funding and the sector's thin margins.
notes: One database labels the 2017 round Series A with Index and Felicis leading; most coverage calls it seed, so seed used. Only YC-listed founder is Yinon Weiss; a search result says Sam Corcos and Todd Opalski co-founded, not listed because no opened YC or company source says so. No later rounds found, hence partial. Competitor lists (Openbay, AutoMD, YourMechanic) came only from auto-generated Owler data with no dated source, so the list is empty. AutoNation later acquired RepairSmith (reported 190 million dollars, December 2022) and rebranded it AutoNation Mobile Service. Failure factors are interpretation.
